headline: PILBARA MINERALS UNVEILS $2.6B NPV P2000 PLAN AT DIGGERS — Would Double Pilgangoora To 2M Tonnes/Year; Feasibility Study Due December Quarter 2026
snippet: Pilbara Minerals (ASX: PLS) CEO Dale Henderson used the final day of Diggers & Dealers 2026 in Kalgoorlie to publicly disclose the full P2000 Expansion economics for Pilgangoora: a brownfield capacity doubling to 2 million tonnes per annum with a pre-feasibility NPV of A$2.6 billion, A$1.2 billion capex, and a 55% internal rate of return. The feasibility study underpinning a final investment decision is on track for December quarter 2026 completion, with management flagging accelerated pre-FID spend on detailed engineering and long-lead items in FY27 to shorten the path to approval — a deliberate public commitment at the sector's flagship conference that management expects financing conditions and lithium prices to support a go-decision within the next 12 months.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING DRILLS 4.82 g/t OVER 35.7m AT OWL CREEK — Dome (11Moz), TVZ, Owl Creek Resource Estimates On Track For Late 2026; Projects Target 250-500k oz/yr
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Discovery Mining Ltd.
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV, OTCQX: DSVSF) released August 5 results from 55 drill holes (17,845.5 metres) at its three advanced Porcupine-Timmins growth projects: at Owl Creek 3 km west of Hoyle Pond, highlight drill hole returned 4.82 g/t gold over 35.7 metres and confirmed and expanded mineralization between surface and the 650-metre level; at Dome — host to an existing 11 million ounce Inferred Resource earmarked for a second large-scale Timmins open pit — high-grade zones continued to extend; and at the TVZ underground target, down-plunge potential was confirmed on the 1210 and 1680 levels. Mineral resource estimates for Dome and TVZ are on track for late 2026, and management projects the three growth projects could collectively support 250,000 to 500,000 ounces of additional annual gold production in one of Canada's most established and infrastructure-rich gold districts.

headline: FIREFLY METALS HITS 11.5m @ 13.2% CuEq AT GREEN BAY — 50.4Mt M&I Resource, PEA Due August; A$196M Cash Underpins Newfoundland Copper Development
snippet: FireFly Metals Ltd. (ASX/TSX: FFM) released August 3 the latest underground drill results from its Green Bay Copper-Gold Project in Newfoundland — a 42-hole dataset highlighting 11.5 metres at 13.2% copper equivalent (11.1% Cu, 2.1 g/t Au), alongside 42.0 metres at 6.1% CuEq and 51.5 metres at 4.9% CuEq from the high-grade Core Zone, where nearly 20 million tonnes grading close to 4% CuEq has been defined. With 197,714 metres of underground diamond drilling completed and A$196.4 million in cash, an updated Mineral Resource Estimate (current: 50.4Mt at 2.0% CuEq Measured and Indicated, plus 29.3Mt at 2.5% CuEq Inferred) and a Preliminary Economic Assessment are both targeted for completion by end of August 2026 — the most significant de-risking milestones remaining before a production decision on one of the highest-grade copper systems in Canada.

headline: LAHONTAN GOLD OPENS VOLCANIC-HOSTED ZONE AT SANTA FE MINE — 12.2m @ 1.26 g/t Au At Calvada East; Summit Fault Extends Nevada Oxide District Beyond Known Resources
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSX-V: LG, OTCQB: LGCXF) announced August 5 results from its first focused reverse-circulation drilling campaign at the Santa Fe Mine Project in Walker Lane, Nevada — seven holes totalling 1,990 metres across Calvada East, Slab West, and a deep geophysical test. Hole CAL26-12R returned 12.2 metres at 1.26 g/t gold equivalent oxide at Calvada East, and a separate hole intersected the first significant gold mineralization in Tertiary volcanic rocks along the Summit Fault — a structural target that extends the district's mineralized footprint beyond the defined Slab and Santa Fe resource areas and defines a new exploration avenue in a heap-leach-friendly Nevada oxide jurisdiction where economics are highly attractive at $4,100+ gold.

headline: ECUADOR'S MINING RESET OPENS DOORS — Salazar Resources Defines 1.5km x 0.5km Copper-Gold Porphyry At Monja With 4.77% Cu Rock Chips; Fee Exemption Boosts Exploration Economics
snippet: Salazar Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: SRL) released August 4 an exploration update from its 100%-owned Monja copper-gold porphyry project in Loja Province, southern Ecuador, alongside commentary on Ecuador's improving mining regulatory environment. In under one month, Salazar defined a 1.5 km by 0.5 km copper-gold porphyry mineralized footprint with stockwork veining averaging 10 veins per metre, and rock chip samples returned values up to 4.77% copper and 1.12 g/t gold across the Monja target. Ecuador's new government has implemented a mining fee exemption that materially reduces operating costs for exploration-stage companies — the structural tailwind that was absent during the prior political cycle — positioning early movers in Ecuador's under-explored Lancones Belt copper-gold corridor to accumulate ground ahead of renewed major-company interest in a jurisdiction that sits between Peru's prolific porphyry belt and Colombia's emerging copper discoveries.

headline: GENESIS MINERALS MAPS A$12.6B VAULT MERGER TIMELINE AT DIGGERS — 285koz FY26 At A$2,670 AISC, A$899M Cash Flow; A$2B In Synergies; November Completion Targeted
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) presented at the final day of Diggers & Dealers 2026 in Kalgoorlie on August 5, delivering FY26 results of more than 285,000 ounces at an AISC of A$2,670 per ounce and A$899 million in underlying operating cash flow — then detailing the proposed A$12.6 billion merger with Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) that would create Australia's third-largest listed gold producer at 600,000–700,000 oz per year. CEO Raleigh Finlayson highlighted A$2 billion in projected synergies, with A$715 million from scrapping a planned new Leonora mill and processing through Vault's existing infrastructure; the scheme booklet is targeted for shareholder distribution in August–September 2026, with a November implementation target. For investors watching Australian gold consolidation, Genesis-Vault represents the most significant ASX mining merger of 2026 — combining Tier-1 Western Australian gold operations in a deal that would rank as one of the top-five largest ASX transactions in the resources sector's history.

headline: RESOLUTE MINING FLAGS MALI SECURITY CRISIS AT DIGGERS — Syama Q2 Missed By 10koz As Explosives Access Denied; Permit Delays Expose Structural Supply Chain Risk
snippet: Resolute Mining (ASX: RSG) presented at Diggers & Dealers on August 4 and disclosed that second-quarter gold production at its Syama Mine in Mali came in at approximately 30,000 ounces — 10,000 to 15,000 ounces below the 40,000–45,000 ounce quarterly target — because regional security challenges that emerged in late April and May 2026 compromised road safety and blocked the delivery of explosives critical to underground blasting. Government permit approvals for explosives transportation have been inconsistently granted, leaving the mine intermittently unable to blast on schedule. For investors in Mali-domiciled gold stocks, Resolute's frank disclosure at Diggers is a reminder that the geological and engineering risks at Syama are well-managed, but operating in the Sahel requires managing a sovereign and supply-chain risk that cannot be fully hedged through operational efficiency — a distinction that the market prices into ASX West African gold producers with a persistent discount to NAV.

headline: ALKANE RESOURCES POSTS RECORD A$567M FY26 CASH FLOW AT DIGGERS — A$454M Cash; Maiden Dividend Proposed As Tomingley Beats Guidance At 82,973oz
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) presented at Diggers & Dealers this week with record full-year results: FY26 operating cash flow of A$567 million, a cash, bullion, and liquid investment position of A$454 million, and 168,337 gold equivalent ounces produced at an AISC of A$2,925 per ounce — including Tomingley, which delivered 82,973 ounces, beating its 75,000–80,000 ounce guidance. Alongside the results, Alkane proposed its inaugural dividend — the first in the company's history — marking a shift from pure-reinvestment to shareholder-returns mode in response to record gold margins above A$6,000 per ounce. With the Tomingley underground expansion (A$132 million investment) advancing toward a targeted 100,000 oz/year by FY27, Alkane's Diggers presentation positions it as one of the more attractive yield-generating mid-tier ASX gold stories entering the next phase of the commodity cycle.

headline: TRIDENT RESOURCES ADVANCES La RONGE GOLD BELT DRILL PROGRAM — 6,500m Completed At Contact Lake In 20,000m Campaign; Indigenous Engagement Secured As Assays Pending (TSX-V: TRR)
snippet: Trident Resources Corp. (TSX-V: TRR) reported August 5 that nine holes for 6,500 metres have been completed at the Contact Lake Gold Project in Saskatchewan's La Ronge Gold Belt as part of an anticipated 20,000-metre, approximately 35-hole program, with all current hole assays pending laboratory release. Trident simultaneously announced the appointment of an Indigenous Engagement Consultant — a procedural step that meaningfully advances the social license and permitting pathway for a project that returned 15.11 g/t gold over 51.83 metres (including 42.53 g/t over 4.50 metres) in prior campaigns, establishing the deposit's high-grade potential in a jurisdiction that has produced gold from the La Ronge belt since the 1930s. The program-update timing, coming before assay results, positions Trident for a potential series of high-grade announcements over the coming weeks as Saskatchewan's underexplored gold belt gains renewed investor attention alongside a $4,100 gold price.

headline: CHINA KILLS $5.5B ALLIED GOLD DEAL — Zijin Takes 9.2% Stake At C$32.55 Instead As Regulatory Failure Rewrites China's Global Gold M&A Playbook
snippet: Allied Gold Corporation's planned C$5.5 billion sale to Zijin Gold International collapsed on July 29, 2026 after Chinese regulators failed to approve the transaction before the outside date — despite the deal having cleared Canada, Ethiopia, Mali, and Côte d'Ivoire approvals — causing Allied shares to plunge 18% to C$24.19 on the announcement day. Rather than walk away entirely, Zijin agreed to subscribe for approximately 12.8 million Allied shares at C$32.55 per share (US$295 million total) for a 9.2% strategic stake closing on or about August 10. The collapse of the largest Chinese mining acquisition attempt in Africa since Zijin's own 2024 deal cycle marks a structural shift: Chinese outbound gold M&A — worth more than US$20 billion in announcement value over 2025-2026 — is now operating in a de facto regulatory constraint environment that is reshaping who acquires African gold producers and at what premium.
